neighbours.label: the word piece that follows an '-ick' piece: bick|ering, Nick|i, thick|ened, flick|ering
fire: We could hear the neighbors bickering through the thin wall.
The candles kept flickering during the long dinner.
Vicki brought a cake to the office on Friday.
The gravy thickened nicely after a few minutes.
My cousin Ricki moved to Denver last spring.
The fog was thickening over the bay by noon.
Endless bickering stalled the meeting for an hour.
A flickering streetlight lit the corner of the block.
quiet: We could hear the neighbors arguing through the thin wall.
The candles kept burning during the long dinner.
Nick brought a cake to the office on Friday.
The gravy was thick after a few minutes.
My cousin Rick moved to Denver last spring.
The fog was darkening over the bay by noon.
Endless arguing stalled the meeting for an hour.
A broken streetlight lit the corner of the block.

notes: Layer 0. Card: 'ering' x5 (bick|ering), 'i' x4 (Nick|i), 'ened' (thick|ened), 'ickle'. Probe: 'bicker' (b|icker) also fired 0.64, so the '-ick' context seems to matter. Near misses use the stem alone or other stems with the same endings. Tokenization checked.
